title: Adaptive Integrity Onboarding Pipeline for OSS LLMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Build an end-to-end adaptive integrity pipeline to onboard new open-source LLM weights into Redwood's catalog. This ticket covers weight intake, format conversion, deterministic validation, variant generation, performance profiling (latency/cost/quality), pin recommendation, and publishing a verified model artifact with canonical metadata and rollback hooks. The aim is to reduce manual handoffs, surface incompatible artifacts early, and automatically produce a publishable model package with a recommended version pin and runtime tuning suggestions.

Scope: ingest raw artifacts from community sources (Hugging Face, Git LFS, direct upload), run deterministic conversions to our canonical runtime format, execute fast (smoke) and deep (profiling) validations, generate quantization/variant candidates, compute a profile with cost/latency/quality metrics, and write a publish manifest to the model catalog. The pipeline must emit telemetry for failure modes, attach deterministic checksums and provenance, and support safe revert/pin changes via the catalog control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Raw weight archives can be ingested from HF/Git LFS and stored in the artifact store with provenance metadata
Automated converter produces a canonical runtime artifact with deterministic byte signatures for a given input
Smoke validation (sanity forward pass + KV cache smoke) passes within 2 minutes for baseline models
Profiling harness runs and populates a performance profile (p50/p95 latency, GPU memory, token throughput, estimated cost per 1k tokens)
Pin recommendation engine returns a preferred pin and at least one compatible fallback variant
Publishing step writes model entry to catalog with metadata, profile, and links to artifacts; CI guard prevents publish if safety/signature checks fail
Pipeline emits structured telemetry events for each stage and captures failure reasons to Sentry/observability dashboards
updates: 2026-02-15 - Aisha Patel: Initial design doc linked and core acceptance criteria agreed with PM. Decided to prioritize deterministic converters for HF transformers first.

2026-02-20 - Marco Li: Prototype converter implemented for 'hf-transformer' -> 'redwood-canonical' with unit tests. Observed nondeterminism for layernorm dtype casting on CPU; added deterministic seeding step.
2026-02-26 - Infra: Storage schema updated to include 'provenance.v1' metadata bucket (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/artifacts/pull/421).
2026-03-03 - Design review: Catalog metadata contract approved; requires 'recommended_pin', 'compatible_variants', 'profiling_snapshot' fields. Frontend expects profiling_snapshot URL.

2026-03-08 - Marco Li: Integrated lightweight profiling harness that runs 100-token generation with 8 concurrent samples; p50 latency baseline reported. Still tuning GPU memory sampling on multi-GPU configs.

2026-03-10 - QA: Added a regression test that compares converter output checksums against reference for a small subset of community models. Edge case: models using custom rotary embeddings need special mapping; added adapter rule.
comments: Marco Li (2026-02-21): Noted a trade-off: deterministic conversion adds ~20% runtime to the conversion step but avoids flaky profiles downstream. Recommend running deterministic conversion in a cheap CPU conversion pool to limit cost.
Sofia Martinez (PM, 2026-02-28): Prioritize HF 'transformers' and 'llama' community weights first due to customer demand. Add a gated list for experimental formats.
Jamal Reynolds (Security, 2026-03-04): Add a signature verification step and require provenance manifest for external weights. If manifest missing, mark as 'manual review' in catalog.
Elliot Park (DX, 2026-03-09): Request exposing the recommended quantization profile in the published metadata so customers can opt-in for a lower-cost variant via the API.
implementation_notes: Split pipeline into independent stages: ingest -> convert -> smoke-validate -> profile -> pin-recommend -> publish; each stage writes a well-defined artifact to S3 with schema v1
Use feature-flagged path: 'fast-path' for smoke-only onboarding to accelerate initial publish for small models (<4B)
Converter must track ABI compatibility and include a mapping table for custom ops (adapter plugins)
Profiling harness supports deterministic seeds for generation and collects token-level latencies and memory high-water marks
Pin recommendation uses weighted scoring: reliability (40%), perf delta (30%), cost delta (20%), safety checks (10%)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Community weights with nonstandard tensor names can break converter - Mitigation: build adapter registry and provide a fallback interactive mapping tool for solutions engineers
Risk: Profiling on limited hardware misestimates memory for production GPU families - Mitigation: include hardware-normalization factors and conservative headroom in recommendations
Risk: Publishing a model with undiscovered safety issues - Mitigation: enforce a safety-signature gate; models failing automated safety checks are routed to manual review
